canonical_title: US Commerce Department requires export licenses for advanced AI chips to third-country data centers
aliases: Singapore Malaysia Thailand Indonesia Brazil export licenses
Nvidia Southeast Asia server shipment pause
treatment: New binding rule, distinct from November 13 regional scrutiny. Follow up only for official text, effective date, exemptions or enforcement changes.
known_facts: Reuters November 16 13:46 UTC reports a new US rule requiring export license applications for advanced AI chips in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil.
Commerce Department aims to prevent circumvention through remote computing in third-country data centers.

Nov 26 Reuters 07:19 UTC: anonymous sources say GLM-5.5 may slip into Q1 2027 or later; Moonshot major release cycles could double if overseas compute is lost. Anti-distillation measures are also cited. No official revised launch dates.

Nov 26 Reuters 05:09 UTC citing FT: Nvidia reportedly directed partners to pause server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries; duration and official company confirmation unknown. Rule effective Nov 19.
reinclude_only_if: Official rule text or implementation date changes
notes: Published after November 16 midday; Nov13 coverage concerned possible regulation, not this issued rule.
